gap: No result ChatGPT got says that one link, Sun Gold Power's SGR-8K10E at $4,949 on 2026-11-13, puts an entire 48 V off-grid set in one cart: an 8 kW 120/240 V inverter with a built-in dual MPPT, 2 × 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 batteries that talk to it over RS485, 8 × 450 W panels, and the DC/PV breakers, 2/0 AWG cables and busbar. It also doesn't say that this 3.6 kW of panels uses only about a third of the inverter's stated 11,000 W PV input, while the kit ships with one 25 A PV breaker and one 50 ft PV extension set, so adding panels on the second MPPT means buying a second breaker and cable set.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chats list no search results and no cited pages, so there is no rival page to compare. I compared against its answer text only. That text describes the general layout (panels, MPPT, LiFePO4, inverter, breakers), says a 48 V system with an all-in-one inverter/charger suits builds above about 3 kW, and gives budget ranges ($5,000–$10,000 for a medium cabin). It never names a single-cart kit, a real price, the parts list, the inverter-to-battery RS485 link, or the fact that the kit's PV gear covers only one of the inverter's two MPPT inputs. The kit only fills the cart. It does not decide which set to buy, so I rated it 2, not 3.
kit_items: Inverter/charger with built-in MPPT: Sun Gold Power 8KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter (in SGR-8K10E). Gives 120/240 V split-phase output with 2 built-in MPPTs and up to 500 VDC open-circuit PV input per the store listing, so no separate charge controller is needed.
Battery: 2 × Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah server-rack LiFePO4 (10.24 kWh, UL1973/UL9540A). Matches the 48 V inverter and talks to it over RS485.
Panels: 8 × Sun Gold Power SGN-450-BDG5 450 W bifacial N-type (3.6 kW, Vmp 30.08 V per the kit page).
Protection and wiring: included in the kit (200 A DC breaker, 25 A PV breaker, 2 sets of 2/0 AWG cables, 250 A busbar, 50 ft PV extension set, 8 sets of Z-brackets).
Second-MPPT expansion (optional, not in the kit): a second PV breaker and PV extension cable set if you add panels on MPPT 2.

I couldn't confirm the per-panel price, so I can't prove the kit is cheaper than buying the parts. It is the only SKU that fills the whole set in one cart, so the kit is the item to use. No free gift is listed.
